**Synopsis:**
As of September 1, 2026, European markets are under significant stress heading into autumn: benchmark gas prices are at 3.5-year highs, bond futures (Bunds, OATs) are at multi-year lows, and French/German yields are at 15-year peaks. A European rate hike is expected next week. Globally, the Iran war is disrupting Qatar gas supply and prompting further US military engagement. US 10-year Treasury yields hit a 20-month high, driven by a mix of rising real yields and term premium expansion — the NY Fed's term premium measure more than tripled since January 2025. Japan's 10-year yield touched 3% for the first time since 1996. Equities are broadly lower across Asia. Key data points due: Eurozone CPI, US JOLTS, ISM Manufacturing; earnings from Dell and Palo Alto Networks.

Sentiment: +55 — decidedly hawkish tilt. US 10-year yields at a 20-month high, term premium having more than tripled since January 2025, and the rise in yields outpacing breakeven inflation (suggesting real yield/term premium drivers rather than just inflation) all point to a market pricing higher-for-longer or upward rate pressure. No dovish signals are present in the article.
